Question Choices: If lim g(x)=2 and f is continuous at 2 what is lim f(g(x))? All limits refer to the same approach x->a. Assume f(g(x)) is defined for all sufficiently close x in the domain.
Hints: Use the composite-function limit theorem.|Pass the inner limit into the continuous outer function.
Solution: If g(x)->L and f is continuous at L, then f(g(x))->f(L), provided the composition is defined nearby. Discontinuity at L prevents automatic substitution but does not force failure of the composite limit. The theorem is sufficient, not necessary: a varying inner function can be mapped to a constant outer value. The limit is f(2).
